stem: Local self-government in large cities is carried out by a:
solution: Large urban areas (big cities) are governed by Municipal Corporations.

stem: Which urban local body governs a smaller town?
solution: Smaller towns are administered by a Municipality (Municipal Council); the largest cities have Municipal Corporations.

stem: The elected head of a Municipal Corporation is the:
solution: The Mayor is the elected head of a Municipal Corporation. The Municipal Commissioner is the appointed administrative officer.

stem: Elected members of a Municipal Corporation who represent different wards of a city are called:
solution: Councillors (ward members) are elected from each ward of a city to the Municipal Corporation.

stem: Which of the following is a typical responsibility of an urban local body?
options: Garbage collection, water supply and street maintenance
solution: Urban local bodies manage civic services such as garbage disposal, water supply, drainage, streetlights and local roads.

stem: Municipal bodies raise money to provide services mainly through:
options: Taxes such as property tax and various fees
solution: Urban local bodies fund services largely through local taxes (like property tax), user charges and grants.

stem: The appointed administrative officer who implements the decisions of a Municipal Corporation is the:
solution: The Municipal Commissioner, an appointed official, is responsible for the administration and execution of the Corporation's decisions.

stem: Urban local bodies in India were given constitutional status by which amendment?
solution: The 74TH CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT (1992) gave CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS to URBAN LOCAL BODIES (municipalities). (The 73rd Amendment did the same for rural panchayats.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: The three main types of urban local bodies in India are the Municipal Corporation (big cities), the Municipality/Municipal Council (towns), and the:
solution: The three main URBAN LOCAL BODIES are the MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (large cities), the MUNICIPALITY/MUNICIPAL COUNCIL (towns), and the NAGAR PANCHAYAT (for transitional/small urban areas moving from rural to urban). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'ward' in a city is:
options: A division of the city from which a councillor is elected
solution: A WARD is a DIVISION of the CITY from which a COUNCILLOR (ward member) is ELECTED to the municipal body. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a civic service provided by urban local bodies?
options: Water supply, sewage, garbage disposal, street lighting and parks
solution: URBAN LOCAL BODIES provide CIVIC SERVICES like WATER SUPPLY, SEWAGE, GARBAGE DISPOSAL, STREET LIGHTING, roads, and PARKS — the everyday needs of city life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Mayor of a Municipal Corporation is:
options: Elected and acts as the ceremonial and elected head
solution: The MAYOR is ELECTED and acts as the CEREMONIAL and ELECTED HEAD of the Municipal Corporation, presiding over its meetings. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Mayor — elected head of a corporation 2. Municipal Commissioner — appointed administrative officer. How many are correctly matched?
solution: BOTH pairs are correct: the MAYOR is the ELECTED HEAD of a Municipal Corporation, and the MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER is the APPOINTED ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER who runs its day-to-day work. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The main source of income for urban local bodies is:
options: Property tax and other local taxes, fees and grants
solution: URBAN LOCAL BODIES earn income mainly from PROPERTY TAX and other LOCAL TAXES, user FEES (for water, etc.), and GRANTS from the state and central governments. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a difference between rural and urban local government?
options: Rural areas have Panchayati Raj; urban areas have municipalities/corporations
Urban areas have no local government
solution: A key difference is that RURAL areas have the PANCHAYATI RAJ system, while URBAN areas have MUNICIPALITIES and MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS — different structures suited to their needs. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The councillors of a Municipal Corporation are chosen by:
options: Election by the people of each ward
solution: COUNCILLORS are chosen by ELECTION by the PEOPLE of each WARD, making them accountable to the residents they represent. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Reservation of seats in urban local bodies is provided for:
options: Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
solution: Like panchayats, URBAN LOCAL BODIES reserve seats for WOMEN, SCHEDULED CASTES, and SCHEDULED TRIBES, ensuring representation of these groups. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of a municipality regarding public health?
options: Maintaining cleanliness, controlling disease and running local dispensaries
solution: Regarding PUBLIC HEALTH, a MUNICIPALITY MAINTAINS CLEANLINESS, helps CONTROL DISEASE (e.g., through vaccination drives and sanitation), and runs LOCAL DISPENSARIES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why do cities need local government?
options: Cities have large populations and complex needs that require local management of services
Cities govern themselves without any body
solution: CITIES need LOCAL GOVERNMENT because they have LARGE POPULATIONS and COMPLEX NEEDS (water, sanitation, traffic, housing) that require LOCAL MANAGEMENT of services. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which body would govern a metropolitan city like Mumbai or Delhi?
solution: A large METROPOLITAN CITY like Mumbai or Delhi is governed by a MUNICIPAL CORPORATION, the urban body for the biggest cities. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The elected councillors and the appointed commissioner work together to:
options: Make and carry out decisions for running the city
solution: The ELECTED COUNCILLORS (who make policy) and the APPOINTED COMMISSIONER (who implements it) work TOGETHER to MAKE and CARRY OUT DECISIONS for running the city. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a municipal function related to city infrastructure?
options: Building and maintaining roads, bridges, drains and markets
solution: A MUNICIPAL function related to INFRASTRUCTURE is BUILDING and MAINTAINING ROADS, BRIDGES, DRAINS, and MARKETS within the city. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The property tax collected by a municipality is used to:
options: Fund civic services and city development
solution: PROPERTY TAX collected by a municipality is used to FUND CIVIC SERVICES (water, sanitation, roads) and CITY DEVELOPMENT for the benefit of residents. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Urban local government helps residents by:
options: Bringing decision-making about city services closer to the people
solution: URBAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT helps residents by BRINGING DECISION-MAKING about CITY SERVICES CLOSER to the PEOPLE, so local needs are better understood and met. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A Nagar Panchayat is meant for:
options: Areas that are changing from rural to urban (small/transitional towns)
solution: A NAGAR PANCHAYAT is meant for AREAS CHANGING from RURAL to URBAN — small or transitional towns that are becoming urban but are not yet large enough for a municipality. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches an urban body with the settlement it governs?
options: Municipal Corporation → large city; Municipality → town; Nagar Panchayat → small/transitional town
Municipal Corporation → village; Municipality → metro city; Nagar Panchayat → nation
solution: The correct matches are: MUNICIPAL CORPORATION → LARGE CITY; MUNICIPALITY → TOWN; and NAGAR PANCHAYAT → SMALL/TRANSITIONAL town. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a challenge that urban local bodies must address?
options: Managing waste, traffic, water supply and growing populations
solution: URBAN LOCAL BODIES must address CHALLENGES like managing WASTE, TRAFFIC, WATER SUPPLY, housing, and GROWING POPULATIONS in fast-expanding cities. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The role of citizens in urban governance includes:
options: Voting in local elections, paying taxes, and keeping the city clean
solution: Citizens' ROLE in urban governance includes VOTING in local elections, PAYING TAXES, and helping KEEP the CITY CLEAN and orderly. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Municipal Corporations govern big cities. Reason (R): Big cities have large populations and complex civic needs requiring a well-organised local body. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — Municipal Corporations govern big cities. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: BIG CITIES have LARGE POPULATIONS and COMPLEX civic NEEDS that require a well-organised local body (a corporation) to manage them. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The separation of the elected wing (councillors/Mayor) and the administrative wing (Commissioner) in a corporation ensures that:
options: Policy-making and its implementation are handled by appropriate people
solution: The separation of the ELECTED wing (councillors/Mayor, who MAKE policy) and the ADMINISTRATIVE wing (Commissioner, who IMPLEMENTS it) ensures POLICY-MAKING and IMPLEMENTATION are handled by the APPROPRIATE people. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Local bodies (rural and urban) together form which level of government in India?
options: The third (local) level, below the Union and State
The first level, above all others
solution: Local bodies (panchayats and municipalities) together form the THIRD (LOCAL) LEVEL of government in India, below the UNION and STATE levels. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following would a Municipal Corporation typically NOT do?
solution: A Municipal Corporation would NOT conduct the country's FOREIGN POLICY (a central government job). It DOES collect garbage, supply water, and maintain streetlights. So option 1 is correct.

stem: How often are elections generally held for urban local bodies?
solution: Elections for URBAN LOCAL BODIES are generally held every FIVE YEARS, ensuring regular and accountable local government. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The main aim of both rural and urban local self-government is to:
options: Enable people to manage their own local affairs and development
solution: The main AIM of both RURAL and URBAN local self-government is to ENABLE PEOPLE to MANAGE their OWN LOCAL AFFAIRS and DEVELOPMENT, bringing democracy to the grassroots. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A citizen who notices a broken streetlight or overflowing drain should ideally:
options: Report it to the local municipal body/councillor
solution: A citizen noticing a broken streetlight or overflowing drain should REPORT it to the LOCAL MUNICIPAL BODY or their COUNCILLOR, so the civic problem can be fixed. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The keeping of records such as births, deaths and marriages in a city is done by:
solution: The keeping of RECORDS such as BIRTHS, DEATHS, and MARRIAGES in a city is done by the MUNICIPAL BODY — an important civic function. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best describes how urban local bodies improve city life?
options: By providing clean water, sanitation, roads, lighting and public services
solution: URBAN LOCAL BODIES improve city life by PROVIDING CLEAN WATER, SANITATION, ROADS, LIGHTING, and other PUBLIC SERVICES that make cities liveable. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Good urban governance requires cooperation between:
solution: GOOD URBAN GOVERNANCE requires COOPERATION between ELECTED REPRESENTATIVES (councillors/Mayor), OFFICIALS (Commissioner and staff), and CITIZENS, all working together for the city. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'municipal' relates to:
options: The government of a town or city
solution: The word 'MUNICIPAL' relates to the GOVERNMENT of a TOWN or CITY — hence municipality, municipal corporation, and municipal services. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a benefit of citizens participating in urban governance?
options: Better, more responsive city services and cleaner surroundings
solution: When citizens PARTICIPATE in urban governance (voting, reporting problems, cooperating), the result is BETTER, MORE RESPONSIVE city SERVICES and CLEANER surroundings. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The urban local body responsible for a medium-sized town (not a big city) is the:
solution: A medium-sized TOWN (not a big city) is governed by a MUNICIPALITY / MUNICIPAL COUNCIL. Big cities have corporations; villages have panchayats. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Both the 73rd and 74th Amendments together strengthened Indian democracy by:
options: Giving constitutional status to rural and urban local self-government
solution: The 73RD (rural) and 74TH (urban) Amendments together strengthened democracy by giving CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS to LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT — bringing governance to the grassroots in both villages and cities. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a shared feature of rural and urban local bodies?
options: Elected members, reserved seats, and five-yearly elections
solution: Both rural and urban local bodies share features like ELECTED MEMBERS, RESERVED SEATS (for women, SC, ST), and FIVE-YEARLY ELECTIONS — democratic self-government at the local level. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The town planning and regulation of building construction in a city is done by:
solution: TOWN PLANNING and the REGULATION of BUILDING construction in a city is done by the MUNICIPAL BODY, ensuring orderly and safe urban growth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is it important for urban local bodies to have their own sources of income?
options: So they can independently fund and provide civic services
So they depend entirely on foreign aid
solution: It is important for URBAN LOCAL BODIES to have their OWN SOURCES of INCOME (like property tax) so they can INDEPENDENTLY FUND and PROVIDE civic services without relying entirely on others. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A Cantonment Board is a special type of urban local body that administers:
solution: A CANTONMENT BOARD is a special urban local body that administers MILITARY CANTONMENT (garrison) AREAS, providing civic services to both military and civilian residents there. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The public parks, gardens and playgrounds in a city are usually maintained by:
solution: PUBLIC PARKS, GARDENS, and PLAYGROUNDS in a city are usually maintained by the MUNICIPAL BODY for the recreation and health of residents. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Street vendors, markets and shops in a city are regulated (licensed) by:
solution: STREET VENDORS, MARKETS, and SHOPS in a city are REGULATED and LICENSED by the MUNICIPAL BODY, which manages commercial activity and public spaces. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The management of fire services and disaster response in many cities is linked to:
solution: FIRE SERVICES and DISASTER RESPONSE in many cities are linked to MUNICIPAL and LOCAL GOVERNMENT arrangements, helping keep residents safe in emergencies. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Grassroots Democracy – Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas' is that:
options: URBAN areas are governed by LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT bodies — the MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (large cities), the MUNICIPALITY/MUNICIPAL COUNCIL (towns), and the NAGAR PANCHAYAT (small/transitional towns) — given constitutional status by the 74th Amendment; each has ELECTED members (COUNCILLORS) and an elected head (MAYOR in a corporation) who make decisions, and an appointed MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER who implements them; these bodies provide civic services like water, sanitation, garbage disposal, roads, lighting and health, funded by local taxes (property tax) and grants, hold elections every five years and reserve seats for women, SCs and STs — bringing democracy and self-government to city life
Citizens have no role in cities
solution: The chapter's overall message is that URBAN areas are governed by LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT bodies — the MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (for large cities), the MUNICIPALITY/MUNICIPAL COUNCIL (for towns), and the NAGAR PANCHAYAT (for small/transitional towns) — which were given CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS by the 74TH AMENDMENT (1992). Each body has ELECTED MEMBERS (COUNCILLORS, elected from wards) and, in a corporation, an elected head (the MAYOR) who MAKE decisions, along with an appointed MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER who IMPLEMENTS them. These bodies provide CIVIC SERVICES like WATER, SANITATION, GARBAGE DISPOSAL, ROADS, LIGHTING, and HEALTH, funded by LOCAL TAXES (especially PROPERTY TAX) and GRANTS; they hold ELECTIONS every FIVE YEARS and RESERVE seats for WOMEN, SCs, and STs — bringing DEMOCRACY and SELF-GOVERNMENT to city life. So the overall message is option 2.
